title: A recursive function stops by itself
statement: A recursive function stops calling itself when there is nothing left to do, so it does not need an explicit base case.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict the behaviour of a recursive function with no base case
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts termination with a sensible answer

example.expected: 3 2 1 0 -1 ... until the recursion limit is hit

if n == 0: return 1
return n * factorial(n - 1)

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip is one forgotten base case the learner adds when asked how it stops. The belief is the answer 'it stops when n runs out'.

vs.prog.func.recursion-as-loop: Loop-model holders often include a base case but expect only one copy of the variables; base-case omitters expect the function to stop on its own.

conflicts_with.label: A recursive function stops only when a base case returns

resolved_by.label: A recursive function stops only when a base case returns
Each recursive call has its own activation with its own variables
